content.overview: Hindu minority and guardianship is governed primarily by the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956. Core modules: natural guardians (s. 6); powers of natural guardian (s. 8); welfare of the minor as paramount consideration (s. 13). Undivided interest in joint family property is excluded from natural guardianship of property under s. 6.
content.glance: Route: who is guardian → s. 6; what powers → s. 8; court decision → s. 13 welfare.
content.study:

sections.heading: Natural guardians — s. 6
sections.body: Father then mother (legitimate); mother then father (illegitimate); husband (married girl); proviso for conversion/renunciation.

sections.heading: Powers — s. 8
sections.body: Acts for benefit of minor; no personal covenant; immovable alienations need court permission.

sections.heading: Welfare — s. 13
sections.body: Paramount in court appointment/declaration; can override bare statutory claim.

sections.heading: Exclusion
sections.body: Undivided joint-family interest outside s. 6 property guardianship.

sections.heading: Routing tip
sections.body: Identify status first, then powers, then welfare if court is involved.

examples.title: Routing
examples.body: Custody dispute in court — apply s. 6 order then s. 13 welfare.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 6 alone decide every guardianship case?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. When the court appoints or declares a guardian, s. 13 welfare is paramount.

distinctions.title: s. 6 natural order vs s. 13 welfare

misconceptions.trap: Father always wins custody under HMGA.
misconceptions.correction: s. 13 makes welfare paramount in court decisions.
